title: 1896 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship
text:
{{Short description|10th series of All Ireland Senior Hurling Championship}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1896 | image = | dates = | teams = | connacht = | munster = Tipperary | leinster = Dublin | ulster = | matches = | poty = | team = Tipperary | titles = 3rd | captain = [[Mikey Maher]] | manager = | team2 = Dublin | captain2 = [[Pat Buckley (Dublin hurler)|Pat Buckley]] | manager2 = | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1895|1895]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1897|1897]] }} The '''All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1896''' was the tenth series of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], [[Ireland]]'s premier [[hurling]] [[single-elimination tournament|knock-out competition]]. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] won the championship, beating [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] 8–14 to 0–4 in the [[1896 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=25 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }} ==Rule change== At the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s (GAA) annual congress it was decided to change the value of a goal. From 1892 until 1896 a goal was worth five points; however, the new change resulted in a goal being worth three points. ==Format== '''All-Ireland Championship''' ''Final:'' (1 match) The two provincial representatives made up the two final teams with the winners being declared All-Ireland champions. ==Provincial championships== ===[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{footballbox |date=Semi-final |team1=[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |score=w.o – scr. |team2=[[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium= |attendance= |referee= }} ---- {{footballbox |date=23 May 1897
Final |team1=[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |score=1–8 – 0–6 |team2=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Jones' Road]], [[Dublin]] |attendance= |referee= |event=|time=|round=|score1=|score2=|penaltyscore=|penalties1=|penalties2=|location=|aet=}} An objection was made and a replay ordered. ---- {{footballbox |date=27 February 1898
Final replay |team1=[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |score=4–6 – 0–0 |team2=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium= |attendance= |referee= |event=|time=|round=|score1=|score2=|penaltyscore=|penalties1=|penalties2=|location=|aet=}} ===[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{footballbox |date=Semi-final |team1=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] |score=5–1 – 0–1 |team2=[[Clare GAA|Clare]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Kilmallock]] |attendance= |referee= |event=|time=|round=|score1=|score2=|penaltyscore=|penalties1=|penalties2=|location=|aet=}} ---- {{footballbox |date=Semi-final |team1=[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |score=2–5 – 1–2 |team2=[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Tipperary (town)|Tipperary]] |attendance= |referee= |event=|time=|round=|score1=|score2=|penaltyscore=|penalties1=|penalties2=|location=|aet=}} ---- {{footballbox |date=Final |team1=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] |score=1-3 – 1-3 |team2=[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Kilmallock]] |attendance= |referee= }} ---- {{footballbox |date=Final replay |team1=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] |score=7–9 – 2–3 |team2=[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Croke Park|Jones's Road]], [[Dublin]] |attendance= |referee= |event=|time=|round=|score1=|score2=|penaltyscore=|penalties1=|penalties2=|location=|aet=}} ---- ==All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship== ===Final=== {{footballbox |date=27 March 1898
Final |team1=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] |score=8–14 – 0–4 |team2=[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Croke Park|Jones's Road]], [[Dublin]] |attendance=c.8,000 |referee= D. Wood (Dublin) |event=|time=|round=|score1=|score2=|penaltyscore=|penalties1=|penalties2=|location=|aet=}} ---- ==Championship statistics== ===Miscellaneous=== * The Munster final ended in a draw for the first time ever. A replay was played for the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Championship|1891 Munster final]]; however, this was due to an objection rather than a draw. * The Leinster final went to a replay as [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] launched an objection against [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]. * [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] became the second team to win back-to-back All-Ireland titles following their final victory over Dublin. [[Mikey Maher]] became the first person to captain two All-Ireland-winning teams. ==References== {{reflist}} ==Sources== * Corry, Eoghan, ''The GAA Book of Lists'' (Hodder Headline Ireland, 2005). * Donegan, Des, ''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' (DBA Publications Limited, 2005). {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships|1896]] [[Category:1896 in Irish sport]]
